objective: One bounded read-only operational cross-section of the current SparkBrain scheduler-delay pattern, using a fresh live scheduler timing snapshot plus durable worker timestamps to test whether the prior broad queue-pressure diagnosis persists or instead localizes to a deterministic phase/role.
finding_summary: Broad coarse lateness persisted in a fresh scheduler window, so the prior delay observation was not isolated to one window.
The fresh durable MAIN lease started at 02:16:01 JST for a nominal :15 phase, an exact start offset of about +1m01, then remained active until blocked at 02:21:30.
Large coarse offsets on Brief/Analyst coexist with a near-phase exact MAIN start and smaller Relay offset, weakening a simple monotonically accumulating five-minute phase-cascade explanation.
Role runtime heterogeneity and/or shared scheduler/backend queue pressure remain plausible; no exact deterministic collision or evidence-based single phase target was established.
Live scheduler last_run_time is not authoritative started_at/queued_at telemetry and may represent completion/recording; exact worker timestamps should be preferred when available.

freshness_check_before_terminal_persiste.relay: NO_SEPARATE_ACTIVE_RELAY_OWNERSHIP; MAIN state remained BLOCKED pending fresh Analyst review

follow_up_recommendation: Before any scheduler timing mutation, collect exact nominal_due_at/queued_at/started_at/finished_at-or-blocked_at telemetry for at least three comparable dense windows. Prefer durable started_at/terminal timestamps over coarse scheduler last_run_time where available. No duplicate Utility request was added because Control already owns scheduler-health decisions and persistent-delay observation.
